newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh rebels kill three police.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh rebels kill three police.

text.p: Suspected tribal rebels in the Chittagong Hill Tracts of southwestern Bangladesh on Saturday killed three policemen in an ambush, police said.

They said the insurgents fired on six policemen patrolling a road in the guerrilla-infested Roangchari area near the border with Indian state of Mizoram, 60 miles (100 km) from Chittagong. Three of the policemen died on the spot and three fled unhurt.

Security sources have blamed a hardline group within the Shanti Bahini (peace force) opposing a peace intiative taken by the government and the Parbatya Chittagram Jana Sanghati Samity (PCJSS), the political wing of the Bahini, to end the decades-old tribal insurgency.
"This is a clear attempt to thwart the current peace process," one police officer.
Officials say the two sides made progress in settling the dispute at a meeting in the capital of Dhaka last month. Another such meeting is due on March 12.

Tribal insurgents have been fighting a bush war for autonomy for 5,500 sq miles (14,200 sq kms) of hill tracts bordering India and Burma. They also want some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers expelled from the area.
Officials say more than 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency since 1973.
